rules.task_completion: All acceptance criteria satisfied, required evidence attached, and reviewer transition to accepted.
rules.dependency: A task may start only when all depends_on items are accepted.
rules.risk_gate: External publication, spending, secrets, destructive actions, and production changes require scoped owner approval.

tasks.title: Approve baseline and capture environment
tasks.outcome: Approved scope revision and supported-machine profile exist.
acceptance: Owner approves product spec, architecture, agent contract, and delivery plan at exact revisions.
Record Windows machine architecture, macOS M1 Max target, initial harness preference, and any provider constraints.
verification: Inspect signed-off decision register and scope revision.

tasks.title: Validate Rust desktop UI toolkit
tasks.outcome: A native Rust prototype renders the specified layout responsively.
acceptance: Resizable portfolio, management, and terminal areas work.
Keyboard navigation, text scaling, high DPI, and large project/task list are evaluated.
Document accessibility limitations and recommendation.
verification: Run prototype on Windows; record UI checklist. Repeat on M1 Max before release.

tasks.title: Validate cross-platform terminal
tasks.outcome: Interactive native PTY prototype works on Windows and is designed for macOS validation.
acceptance: Launch native shell in a selected directory.
Input, output, ANSI color, Unicode, resize, scrollback, and exit work.
No shell process remains after tab close or app exit.
verification: Manual PTY matrix on Windows and automated parser tests; repeat on M1 Max before release.

tasks.title: Validate harness integration surfaces
tasks.outcome: Capability matrix for OpenCode and Pi against installed/tested versions.
acceptance: Probe versions and start, event, stop, and recovery behavior.
Record permission and diff event semantics.
Identify unsupported capabilities and fallback behavior.
verification: Run minimal adapter experiments on Windows; repeat process-launch check on M1 Max before release.

tasks.title: Create Rust workspace and CI
tasks.outcome: Modular Rust application builds on primary platforms and Linux CI.
acceptance: Workspace separates domain, store, engine, adapters, terminal, API, app, and CLI concerns.
Formatting, linting, tests, and builds pass locally on Windows; a three-OS CI workflow is configured.
Native app launches with version/about view.
verification: Inspect three-OS CI workflow; execute the matrix before P19 acceptance

tasks.title: Implement persistent domain and audit
tasks.outcome: Project records survive restart and upgrades with a complete activity trail.
acceptance: Versioned SQLite schema implements core entities and foreign keys.
Mutations and activity events commit atomically with optimistic revision checks.
Backup, restore, export, and migration rollback/failure behavior are documented.

tasks.title: Create and import projects
tasks.outcome: Owner sees real projects and accurate portfolio status.
acceptance: Create from folder and import existing Git repository without changing source files.
Path validation handles Windows and macOS conventions.
Portfolio shows stage, health, verified completion, blockers, and next owner action.
verification: Import two sample repositories on Windows; run persistence tests; repeat import on M1 Max before release

tasks.title: Build three-pane desktop shell and terminal tabs
tasks.outcome: Selected project, management workspace, and working shell coexist.
acceptance: Panels resize/collapse and remember state.
Shell starts in selected project folder and terminal tabs remain distinct.
Long output does not freeze the UI.
verification: M1 Max smoke test before release

tasks.title: Build idea intake, research, and brief approval
tasks.outcome: A rough idea becomes a versioned, reviewable product brief.
acceptance: Guided intake captures audience, problem, constraints, and desired outcome.
Research distinguishes sourced facts from hypotheses.
Approval binds to an exact brief revision and changes produce visible deltas.

tasks.title: Build task graph and verified completion
tasks.outcome: Approved work has executable dependencies and measurable progress.
acceptance: Epics, tasks, criteria, weights, and dependency edges can be edited and reviewed.
Cycles are rejected; blocked dependencies prevent scheduling.
Completion counts only accepted weighted work in approved scope and updates after scope revision.

tasks.title: Build decisions, inbox, and review history
tasks.outcome: Owner can inspect and act on every material decision.
acceptance: Decisions show alternatives, rationale, evidence, impact, actor, and supersession.
Inbox prioritizes blockers/high impact and supports revision-bound approve/reject/edit.
Portfolio, milestone, task, and action views link to the same underlying records.

tasks.title: Implement scoped agent write API and CLI
tasks.outcome: Agents can read and update project state without direct database access.
acceptance: Loopback-only API and CLI implement the agent contract operations.
Short-lived scoped tokens, idempotency, revision conflicts, path validation, and audit are enforced.
Invalid, cross-project, stale, or replayed mutations are rejected.

tasks.title: Implement scheduler, isolation, and policy engine
tasks.outcome: Only approved, unblocked work runs in a recoverable checkout.
acceptance: Run state machine enforces preflight and one active code-changing run per project.
Git worktree lifecycle preserves partial work on failure.
Risky actions request scoped approval; denied actions stay denied after retries/restart.
Interrupted runs reconcile on restart without replaying external effects.

tasks.title: Implement OpenCode adapter
tasks.outcome: OpenCode sessions can execute scoped tasks with observable events.
acceptance: Probe, start, stream, steer, stop, and recover map to normalized run events.
Permission requests map to the app policy without auto-approval.
Version mismatch and server outage yield explicit degraded states.
verification: M1 Max session smoke test before release

tasks.title: Complete agent task and evidence review loop
tasks.outcome: Owner can run and accept a real agent-produced task with traceable evidence.
acceptance: Task packet includes approved scope and stop conditions.
Live run, diff, decisions, tests, and artifacts appear in review UI.
Agent submission cannot self-accept; missing evidence prevents acceptance.
Owner can request changes and rerun safely.
verification: End-to-end sample app task on Windows

tasks.title: Implement Pi RPC adapter
tasks.outcome: Pi can perform the same task loop through its JSONL subprocess protocol.
acceptance: Strict LF-delimited framing handles Unicode and partial reads.
Probe, start, events, steer, stop, and recovery declare actual supported capabilities.
Task and policy semantics match OpenCode's normalized contract.
verification: M1 Max task run before release

tasks.title: Add design, UX, and asset review workflows
tasks.outcome: Design work is visible and reviewable alongside code tasks.
acceptance: Flows, wireframes, screenshots, component notes, copy, assets, and accessibility reviews can be linked to tasks and decisions.
Artifact hashes and provenance are displayed.
Approval or revision requests preserve prior versions.

tasks.title: Add release candidate and deployment record
tasks.outcome: A release has reproducible provenance and explicit owner control.
acceptance: Candidate binds version, commit, builds, checks, target, and rollback plan.
Failed required check blocks release approval.
Manual deployment and smoke result can be recorded; production execution requires separate scoped approval.
verification: Sample release with failed then passing check

tasks.title: Add launch, marketing, feedback, and operations workflows
tasks.outcome: Work after code completion remains in the same project timeline.
acceptance: Positioning, launch copy/assets, channel plans, metrics, feedback, bugs, incidents, and maintenance tasks are supported.
External publication remains approval-gated.
Portfolio health reflects release and operations blockers.

tasks.title: Harden and package primary-platform release
tasks.outcome: A reliable installable Windows and Apple Silicon macOS release candidate.
acceptance: Install/launch, onboarding, import, terminal, agent run/recovery, review, export, and manual release flow pass on both primary OSes.
Windows, Apple Silicon macOS, and Linux CI build/tests pass from the project's own remote.
Migration/restore, large-output performance, secret redaction, accessibility, and documentation gates pass.
Known distribution signing/notarization limitations are documented and owner approves release candidate.
